plan.title: Heart total-RNA treated vs control DE (DESeq2)
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single gene-level count matrix (12000 genes x 12 samples, counts.csv) from Salmon plus a 12-row metadata table carrying one condition column: 6 treated vs 6 control human heart samples, unpaired, one batch. The research question asks only which genes differ between treated and control, so the plan stops at differential expression and its report — no enrichment step is added, since the user did not ask for pathways.

Three data facts drive the method choices. (1) The counts are 'from salmon as delivered' and the record does not state whether the length correction was applied; there are no per-sample quant.sf files and no average transcript-length table in the inputs. The model is therefore fitted on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and the report must state that the length offset is lost and that a shift in isoform usage can masquerade as differential expression. tximport is not run — it imports transcript-level estimates, not a gene table.
(2) The libraries are rRNA-depleted total RNA, so T1S1 adds the rRNA / mitochondrial / intronic-share style QC that a poly(A) library would not need, using whatever proxies the delivered gene-level matrix supports (mitochondrial gene share and, if the annotation permits, residual rRNA-biotype share); where a metric cannot be computed from a gene-level table it is reported as not computable rather than approximated.
(3) QC flags two concerns. sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median: it is kept through QC, plotted, and its depth and detected-gene count reported; DESeq2 size factors already down-weight it, so removal would be a judgement requiring a stated reason, not a default. Duplication above 60 percent in most libraries: without UMIs the duplicates are not removed, because in RNA-seq duplication tracks expression level and de-duplication would delete true signal. The per-sample duplication rate is reported beside library size and detected genes; a sample with duplication far above the rest in a low-depth library would be flagged as a candidate outlier with a stated reason.

The test is the DESeq2 Wald test on ~ condition with control set explicitly as the reference level, contrast (condition, treated, control), apeglm shrinkage of the reported log2 fold change, independent filtering on, and BH adjustment at alpha 0.05. With 6 per group DESeq2 flags Cook's-distance count outliers and returns NA p-values rather than replacing counts, so the NA classes (outlier vs independent filter) are counted separately. An edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test runs on the same filtered counts and the same design as an independent robustness check; the intersection is the high-confidence set and method-unique genes are reported separately, never the union. n=6 per group with a high duplication rate and one shallow library gives real but modest power — the report states this rather than presenting the gene list as definitive.

median-of-ratios size factors inside the model
~ condition with explicit reference level control
DE report with MA plot, dispersion plot, method overlap, session info

Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, package versions, seed, and annotation source is stored with the results
constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep p-values from the unshrunken fit
Do not rank or threshold by the unshrunken fold change alone
Name the shrinkage estimator (apeglm) in the table header
Report the intersection of the two methods, not the union
Do not add enrichment, pathway, or gene-set analysis — it is outside the research question
caveats: Shrinkage changes the reported effect size, not the test; significance still comes from the unshrunken Wald fit
Fold changes must be read with the length-offset caveat attached — an isoform-usage shift can look like differential expression on a gene table with no length correction
With 12000 genes and 12 samples the analysis is modestly powered; report effect sizes with their standard errors rather than fold changes alone

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

If a sample has a high duplication rate, do not remove the duplicate reads unless the library carries unique molecular identifiers. In RNA-seq the duplication rate follows the expression level, because a highly expressed gene gives many identical fragments. Thus removal without UMIs deletes true signal, and it does not improve the differential expression result. Report the duplication rate of each sample beside its library size and its detected genes. A duplication rate far above the others in a low-depth library is a sign of low complexity, and then the sample is a candidate outlier with a stated reason.

A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
